rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Māliki is the active participle meaning owner, read with long ā; the catalog calls it the dominant eastern reading.
rows.anchor: active participle ""owner"" with long ā; the dominant eastern reading

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maliki means king, without long ā, shifting the semantic register from ownership to sovereign office.
rows.anchor: shifts semantic register from ownership to sovereign office

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A canonical substitution of sīn for ṣād changes emphatic to non-emphatic articulation without changing meaning.
rows.anchor: Sīn for ṣād — canonical phonetic substitution; emphatic→non-emphatic, semantic identical

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ishmām reading blends ṣād with zāy, a phonetic intermediate that preserves the same lexeme.
rows.anchor: Intermediate ṣ/z sound (ishmām) — phonetic blend between ṣād and zāy; same lexeme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacing ṣād with sīn leaves the surface meaning unchanged and makes the sound closer to the cognate sabīl.
rows.anchor: same surface meaning but phonetically closer to sabīl cognate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmām colors ṣād with zāy, producing a transitional articulation between ṣ and s.
rows.anchor: ishmām (ṣ with z-color); transitional articulation between ṣ and s

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading lengthens the pronoun vowel through ṣilat al-mīm; it is phonetic.
rows.anchor: lengthened pronoun vowel (silat al-mīm); phonetic variant

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading uses a short ḍamma on the pronoun instead of kasra.
rows.anchor: short ḍamma pronoun vowel instead of kasra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical variant gives the pronoun a ḍamma vowel.
rows.anchor: ḍamma pronoun-vowel variant; canonical

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Form I qadara without shadda permits the senses measuring, determining, estimating, or having ability, beside intensive Form II qaddara.
rows.anchor: Form I qadara allows simple measuring, determining, estimating, or ability, beside intensive Form II qaddara

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten-reading variant has a fuller vowel texture in yusurā while preserving its root and phrase function.
rows.anchor: fuller vowel texture in yusurā; it preserves the same root and phrase function

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb shifts from second-person plural you prefer to third-person plural they prefer, changing the addressee alignment.
rows.anchor: shifts the imperfect verb from second-person plural ""you prefer"" to third-person plural

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reading makes the subject undergo the fire and shifts agency to an implied external causer.
rows.anchor: Canonical passive reading: the subject is made to enter or undergo the fire

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine passive agrees with lāghiyah as the thing heard: no vain utterance is heard there.
rows.anchor: making the clause no vain utterance is heard in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The impersonal or masculine passive presents hearing as an occurrence there, with nominative lāghiyah as the heard item.
rows.anchor: hearing is presented as an occurrence in the place, with lāghiyah nominative as the heard item

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading keeps sīn rather than emphatic ṣād, reducing emphasis while preserving the predicate meaning controller.
rows.anchor: Canonical reading keeps sīn rather than emphatic ṣād, reducing the emphatic coloring

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An intermediate ishmām-like articulation colors the sibilant between ṣād and zāy, with little semantic shift.
rows.anchor: intermediate/ishmām-like articulation colors the sibilant between ṣād and zāy-like voicing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten-reading form doubles yāʾ, preserving the sense of return while changing pronunciation and form texture.
rows.anchor: tightens the vocal pattern with yāʾ doubling, preserving the return sense

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vowel changes watr to witr while preserving the root and foregrounding odd-numbered singularity in the noun pattern.
rows.anchor: shifts watr to witr, preserving و ت ر (w-t-r) while foregrounding odd-numbered singularity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading restores or pronounces final yāʾ in al-wādī, lengthening the word without changing root or syntax.
rows.anchor: restores or pronounces final yāʾ in al-wādī, lengthening the valley word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pause and continuation forms shorten al-wād at pause and pronounce al-wādī in continuation, making final yāʾ recitation-sensitive.
rows.anchor: Canonical pause/continuation form shows a waqf-like shortened al-wād followed by al-wādī

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical reading opens the first-person possessive yāʾ with -a, smoothing its transition into akramani.
rows.anchor: opens or releases the first-person possessive yāʾ with -a, smoothing the transition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading pronounces the first-person suffix with full final yāʾ, making the word for me fuller at the verse ending.
rows.anchor: pronounces the first-person suffix with full final yāʾ, making ""me"" phonetically fuller

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pause form shortens akraman and the connected form restores akramanī, making final yāʾ recitation-sensitive.
rows.anchor: Canonical pause/continuation variant shows a waqf-like shortened akraman followed by full akramanī

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Form II qaddara intensifies measurement: God precisely apportioned or calculated the provision, rather than merely restricting it.
rows.anchor: Canonical Form II reading with doubled dāl intensifies measurement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In connected recitation, the reading opens final yāʾ, fully vocalizing the possessive before ahānani.
rows.anchor: Canonical reading with opened final yāʾ in connected recitation, making the possessive suffix

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A full final first-person yāʾ makes the object pronoun explicit: He humiliated me.
rows.anchor: full final first-person yāʾ, making the object pronoun phonetically explicit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reduced pause and full connected forms preserve the same first-person object, with pause-related yāʾ treatment.
rows.anchor: Canonical pause/connection-related yāʾ treatment; the reduced pause form and full connected form

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefix changes from second-person tu- to third-person yu-, shifting direct address to a report while keeping form and object.
rows.anchor: changes the person prefix from تُـ (tu-, you plural) to يُـ (yu-, they)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Form I taḥuḍḍūna means you urge, reducing the explicit mutual force of Form VI while keeping direct address.
rows.anchor: Canonical reading shifts to Form I 2MP

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Form I yaḥuḍḍūna means they urge and changes direct address to third-person report.
rows.anchor: Canonical reading shifts to Form I 3MP

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb prefix shifts from second-person taʾkulūna to third-person yaʾkulūna, turning direct address into description.
rows.anchor: shifts the verb from 2MP تَأْكُلُونَ (taʾkulūna, you consume) to 3MP يَأْكُلُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefix changes from second-person tu- to third-person yu-, changing the address while retaining the form and object.
rows.anchor: changes the verb prefix from تُـ (tu-, you plural) to يُـ (yu-, they)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive changes the clause from no one punishes as he punishes to no one is punished as he is punished.
rows.anchor: shifting the clause from ""no one punishes"" to ""no one is punished""

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive makes aḥad the affected subject, rather than the active binder, changing he binds to he is bound.
rows.anchor: Canonical passive variant changes Form IV active yūthiqu, he binds, to passive yūthaqu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect stem vowel changes from -sabu to -sibu while the root and interrogative structure remain the same.
rows.anchor: changes the imperfect stem vowel from -sabu to -sibu while preserving the same consonantal root

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten-reading form doubles bāʾ, intensifying the sense of compacting or heaping within the same root field.
rows.anchor: with doubled bāʾ; intensifies the compacting or heaping sense

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical form has kasra in the imperfect stem, preserving root and sense while changing the stem vowel from u to i.
rows.anchor: Canonical vowel variant with kasra in the imperfect stem; it preserves the same consonantal root

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza variant removes the pronounced hamza, smoothing the long-vowel surface while preserving the closed or sealed sense.
rows.anchor: Canonical hamza variant removes the pronounced hamza, yielding a smoother long-vowel surface

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacing wa- with fa- changes coordination into consequence: and so He does not fear.
rows.anchor: replacing wa- with fa-, shifting from coordination to consequence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Assimilating the Form V prefix tāʾ creates a geminate tt, a phonetic intensification matching the semantic intensity.
rows.anchor: Assimilation of the tāʾ: the original Form V tāʾ prefix assimilates

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No variants are reported for this word; canonical readings agree.
rows.anchor: No reported variants for this word — unanimous across canonical readings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pause, Ibn Kathīr and others drop hamza, giving a long final a; this canonical reading softens the command phonetically.
rows.anchor: Ibn Kathir and others drop hamza in pause

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened-vowel form raʾahu contrasts with raʾāhu prosodically and does not change the root meaning.
rows.anchor: The difference is prosodic — shortened alif

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tashīl drops the second hamza in raʾayta; this canonical simplification has no semantic effect.
rows.anchor: the second hamza in ra'ayta is dropped, yielding a-rayta

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza facilitation softens the hamza to an intermediate sound; it is a canonical variant without semantic change.
rows.anchor: Standard variant among the seven readings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madd lengthens the alif before hamza, changing recitation length but preserving the interrogative-perfect structure.
rows.anchor: Extended madd (elongation) on the alif before the hamza

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tashīl softens the hamza in raʾayta to a glide, smoothing the sound without changing meaning.
rows.anchor: the hamza in رَأَيْتَ is softened (tashīl) — the glottal stop is lightened

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This canonical form drops the hamza entirely; Ḥafṣ retains it, and the difference is phonological only.
rows.anchor: The Hafs reading retains the full hamza. No semantic change — purely phonological

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madd lengthens the vowel before yāʾ and adds rhetorical weight while remaining semantically equivalent to Ḥafṣ.
rows.anchor: the extended vowel adds rhetorical weight to the interrogative

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical form among the Seven drops the medial hamza for a smoother pronunciation, with no semantic change.
rows.anchor: drops the medial hamza, yielding a smoother pronunciation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza facilitation with a brief pause preserves the hamza's trace without full pronunciation.
rows.anchor: Hamza facilitation with sakt (brief pause at hamza position)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical madd lengthens ā before hamza and gives the interrogative additional rhythmic weight.
rows.anchor: lengthens the ā before the glottal stop, adding rhythmic weight to the interrogative

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten-reader variant drops hamza and substitutes yāʾ, a recognized dialectal hamza treatment that is semantically identical.
rows.anchor: hamza dropped, yāʾ substituted — khāṭiyatin instead of khāṭiʾatin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Assimilating tāʾ turns the full Form V prefix into a geminate; the meaning stays the same.
rows.anchor: the original tataanazzalu (Form V with full prefix) assimilates the second tāʾ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kasra under lām gives maṭliʿ the alternative mafʿil place-or-time noun pattern; mafʿal and mafʿil are both valid.
rows.anchor: alternative ism makān/zamān pattern (mafʿil); both mafʿal and mafʿil are valid

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ through Abū Jaʿfar reads barīʾa with explicit hamza, deriving it from b-r-ʾ, to create.
rows.anchor: Read by Nāfiʿ (via Abū Jaʿfar)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza reading derives al-barīʾa from the creation root b-r-ʾ, meaning originated beings rather than earth-dwellers.
rows.anchor: explicitly derives from creation root, confirming bariyya = originated beings rather than earth-dwellers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibdāl changes the ṣād phonetics without changing the meaning.
rows.anchor: Phonetic variant in recitation — ibdāl (sound substitution) affecting the ṣād

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard reading gives hāʾ of the pronoun -hu a full long vowel.
rows.anchor: Standard reading with long vowel hāʾ — the pronoun -hu receives full pronunciation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukūn on hāʾ shortens the pronoun and clips the emphatic ending, affecting rhythm but not meaning.
rows.anchor: Canonical variant with sukūn on hāʾ — shortened pronoun, clipped emphatic ending

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard Ḥafṣ reading lengthens the vowel on hāʾ in -hū.
rows.anchor: Long vowel in -hū — hāʾ al-ḍamīr with lengthened vowel, standard Hafs reading

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This canonical form places sukūn on final hāʾ, shortening the pronoun; it is attested in Warsh and others as a pausal form.
rows.anchor: Sukūn on final hāʾ — shortened pronoun, attested in Warsh and other canonical readings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two pausal forms preserve or drop hāʾ al-sakt; the former closes sharply while the latter leaves the vowel open and suspended.
rows.anchor: Two canonical pausal variants: hiyah (with ha' al-sakt preserved) and hiya (with ha' dropped)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive means you will be shown the Fire, making the addressees recipients of divinely caused vision rather than active perceivers.
rows.anchor: Transforms addressees from active perceivers to passive recipients of forced vision

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This canonical variant simplifies hamza into a long vowel, preserving the meaning of sealed; the hamza form has a sharper articulation.
rows.anchor: This is a standard hamza simplification (tashil al-hamz) attested in the reading

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUmud and ʿamad are alternative broken plurals meaning columns; semantic difference is negligible, though ʿumud may sound heavier.
rows.anchor: both are broken plurals of ʿamūd but with different vowel patterns

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened ilāf can be a Form I or shortened Form IV maṣdar; Form I shifts the sense to Quraysh becoming familiar through its own inclination.
rows.anchor: This shifts from Form IV maṣdar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dropping hamza is phonological simplification; the maṣdar remains Form IV, with a smoother flow that the text associates with binding together.
rows.anchor: No change in meaning — the maṣdar remains Form IV — but the phonetic texture becomes smoother

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened ilāf is analyzed as a Form III maṣdar, shifting from Form IV causation to reciprocal familiarity or covenant.
rows.anchor: Form III masdar (mufa'ala pattern) instead of Form IV

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dropping hamza softens the interrogative opening without changing meaning; readers differ on its realization.
rows.anchor: The hamza elision softens the interrogative opening but does not change meaning

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madd lengthens the vowel in place of hamza, making the interrogative opening smoother and more sustained.
rows.anchor: The elongated vowel replaces the glottal stop, creating a smoother but more sustained interrogative opening

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tashīl softens hamza between full realization and elision, an intermediate form among the Seven readers.
rows.anchor: the hamza is softened between full realization and complete elision

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza simplification drops the hamza in shāniʾaka, a canonical phonetic variant with no semantic change.
rows.anchor: This is a phonetic variant within the ten canonical readings — no semantic change

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imāla tilts the initial fatḥa toward kasra, changing the sound but not the morphology or meaning.
rows.anchor: the fatḥa on ʿayn is tilted toward kasra, producing a sound between

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The catalog records the standard Ḥafṣ form and no variants on dīnukum.
rows.anchor: Standard Hafs reading — no variants on this word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard Ḥafṣ form has an open fatḥa on the first-person pronoun yāʾ.
rows.anchor: Standard Hafs reading: wa-liya with open fatha on the ya

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven-reading form has long ī with no final vowel, contrasting phonetically with open liya; both are mutawatir.
rows.anchor: wa-li with long i and no final vowel — the pronoun is closed/silent

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard Ḥafṣ form elides the possessive yāʾ and implies first person through short kasra.
rows.anchor: the 1st person ya elided (hazf) — the possessive is implied by the kasra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restoring the first-person possessive yāʾ makes my dīn explicit and its ownership more emphatic.
rows.anchor: with the full 1st person possessive ya' restored — making the ""my"" explicit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukūn on hāʾ changes lahab to lahb and may shift the sense from the act of flaming to flame as a concrete entity.
rows.anchor: This changes the vowel pattern from fa'al to fa'l

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nominative ḥammālatu can function as predicate or new subject rather than accusative circumstantial or appositional form, identifying her as carrier.
rows.anchor: This transforms the grammatical function: from ḥāl/badal (circumstantial/appositional in accusative)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukūn on fāʾ shortens kufʾan while preserving the root, giving the denial a clipped sound.
rows.anchor: Canonical variant: sukun on fa' (kuf'an instead of kufuwan)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicit hamza makes the root k-f-ʾ visible in writing, unlike standard Ḥafṣ kufuwan with wāw replacing hamza.
rows.anchor: Restores the original radical hamza of k-f-' which is elided in the standard Hafs reading

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eliding the initial hamza of aʿūdhu gives the lām of qul fatḥa for liaison, smoothing the transition into the refuge declaration.
rows.anchor: the hamza of aʿūdhu is dropped and the lam of qul takes a fatha for liaison

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eliding the hamza at the qul/aʿūdhu junction removes the glottal onset for a fluid connection.
rows.anchor: the hamza of aʿūdhu is elided, creating liaison

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No variants are recorded for al-jinna; the word is consistent across canonical readings.
rows.anchor: No recorded variants for this word in this ayah

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains the Day of Judgment as the day God repays servants according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ مالك يوم الدين ﴾ قال يوم يدين الله العباد بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet points to Jews as those under divine anger, in response to a question at Wādī al-Qurā.
rows.anchor: عن بديل العقيلي قال أخبرني عبد الله بن شقيق أنه أخبره من سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بوادي القرى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies Christians as the astray when asked who they are at Wādī al-Qurā.
rows.anchor: قال هؤلاء الضالون يعني النصارى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says ghuthāʾ is decayed matter and aḥwā describes growth that passes through yellow, green, and white before drying.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ غثاء ﴾ قال الغثاء الشيء البالي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Ibn ʿAbbās recited this verse, he would say, ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق عن سعيد بن جبير قال كان ابن عباس إذا قرأ

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib interprets purification as the alms of the fast-breaking festival.
rows.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن أمية عن سعيد بن المسيب في قوله تعالى ﴿ قد أفلح من تزكى ﴾ قال زكاة الفطر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets purification as righteous action.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ قد أفلح من تزكى ﴾ بعمل صالح

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses what is hidden as inner whispering.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يعلم الجهر وما يخفى ﴾ قال الوسوسه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says what this sūra recounts is found in the earlier scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى ﴾ قال إن ما قص الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the faces are humbled in Hell and are laboring and weary there.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ خاشعة عاملة ناصبة ﴾ قال خاشعة في النار

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Seeing a devout, ascetic Christian monk, ʿUmar wept from pity because the monk's effort recalled the verse describing labor in Hell.
rows.anchor: عبد الرزاق عن جعفربن سليمان قال سمعت أبا عمران الجوني يقول مر عمر بن الخطاب براهب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains the spring as having reached its full heat.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ من عين آنية ﴾ قال من عين قد آن حرها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the food called ḍarīʿ as shibriq.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ إلا من ضريع ﴾ قال هو الشبرق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says no falsehood or sin is heard there.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ لاغية ﴾ قال لا يسمع فيها باطل ولا مأثم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses musayṭir as one who subdues or compels.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ بمصيطر ﴾ قال بقاهر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the ten nights as the first ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijja.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وليال عشر ﴾ قال هي العشر الأول من ذي الحجة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the ten nights as the days of Dhū al-Ḥijja completed by God for Moses.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ وليال عشر ﴾ قال هي العشر من ذي الحجة التي أتمها الله لموسى

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masrūq says these are the best days of the year.
rows.anchor: عن مسروق في قوله تعالى ﴿ وليال عشر ﴾ قال هي أفضل أيام السنة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says all creation consists of even and odd, and God swears by creation.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ والشفع والوتر ﴾ قال الخلق كله شفع ووتر

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn says the prescribed prayer includes paired and odd units.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة عن عمران بن حصين قال الصلاة المكتوبة منها شفع ووتر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, as reported by Maʿmar, also says all creation is even and odd.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق وقال معمر وقال الحسن الخلق كله شفع ووتر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima identifies Arafah, the ninth day, as odd and the Sacrifice, the tenth, as even.
rows.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن شروس عن عكرمة قال عرفة وتر والنحر شفع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Iram was a clan of ʿĀd, called Iram of the pillars because its people lived in tents supported by poles.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ بعاد إرم ﴾ قال إرم قبيل من عاد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses their hewing of rock as boring and carving it.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ جابوا الصخر بالواد ﴾ قال نقبوا الصخر نحتوا الصخر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda first glosses Pharaoh's stakes as buildings.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ذي الأوتاد ﴾ قال ذي البناء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda also says they were awnings under which Pharaoh held games and stakes driven for him.
rows.anchor: عبد الرزاق قال أنا معمر عن قتادة قال كانت مظال يلعب له تحتها

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that Pharaoh pegged his wife down by four stakes and placed a great millstone on her back until she died.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت البناني عن أبي رافع قال وتد فرعون لامرأته أربعة أوتاد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God watches the deeds of human beings.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ إن ربك لبالمرصاد ﴾ يقول بمرصاد أعمال بني آدم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says no worldly punishment or binding equals the punishment and binding of that Day.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ فيومئذ لا يعذب عذابه أحد ولا يوثق وثاقه أحد ﴾

rows.speaker: قتادة والحسن
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan describe the tranquil soul as assured by what God has said and affirming it.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ﴾ قال المطمئنة إلى ما قال الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the city in the oath as Mecca.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لا أقسم بهذا البلد ﴾ قال البلد مكة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet is permitted to act in this city and is not sinful there.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأنت حل بهذا البلد ﴾ يقول أنت به حل و لست بآثم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the father and what he fathered as Adam and his offspring.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ووالد وما ولد ﴾ قال آدم وما ولد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses lubadan as abundant wealth.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ مالا لبدا ﴾ قال مالا كثيرا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda warns that a person will be questioned about where wealth was earned and spent.
rows.anchor: عبد الرزاق قال معمر تلا قتادة ﴿ أيحسب أن لم يره أحد ﴾ قال يا ابن آدم

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: A report from Abū Dharr says a servant's feet will not move until asked about four matters: lifespan, body, earnings, and where wealth was spent.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق قال معمر وسمعت رجلا يحدث عن أبي ذر قال لا يتحول قدما عبد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports the Prophet's rhetorical question: the two high roads are good and evil, so why prefer the road of evil?
rows.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ وهديناه النجدين ﴾ قال قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the two high roads as the two breasts.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي أن ابن عباس قال في قوله تعالى ﴿ وهديناه النجدين ﴾ قال الثديين

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd interprets them as the path of good and the path of evil.
rows.anchor: عن زر بن حبيش عن ابن مسعود قال في قوله تعالى ﴿ وهديناه النجدين ﴾ قال سبيل الخير وسبيل الشر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima describes the needy person as so destitute that nothing separates him from the soil he touches.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الكريم بن أبي المخارق عن عكرمة في قوله ﴿ أو مسكينا ذا متربة ﴾ قال ليس بينه وبين التراب شيء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda calls the Fire a barrier before Paradise and explains crossing this obstacle through freeing a slave or feeding someone on a day of famine.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فلا اقتحم العقبة ﴾ قال النار عقبة دون الجنة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima explains al-muttrib as someone stuck to the ground from hardship.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله ﴿ مسكينا ذا متربة ﴾ قال المترب اللازق بالأرض من الجهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses muʾṣada as shut or sealed over.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ مؤصدة ﴾ قال مطبقة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says God made clear to the soul the difference between evil and piety.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فألهمها فجورها وتقواها ﴾ قال قد بين لها الفجور من التقوى

rows.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim glosses the terms as obedience and disobedience.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم في قوله تعالى ﴿ فألهمها فجورها وتقواها ﴾ قال الطاعة والمعصية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the successful person purifies himself through good action, while the failed person buries himself in sin and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ قد أفلح من زكاها ﴾ قال قد أفلح من زكى نفسه بعمل صالح

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda notes that some recitations have al-dhakar wa-l-unthā, ‘the male and the female.’
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وما خلق الذكر والأنثى ﴾ قال في بعض الحروف الذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet had sins weighing heavily on him, which God forgave.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أنقض ظهرك ﴾ قال كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب قد أثقلته

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic explanation says mention of him begins with servanthood and follows with messengership.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ورفعنا لك ذكرك ﴾ أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال بدءا بالعبودية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet is mentioned with the testimony that none is god but God and that Muhammad is God's messenger.
rows.anchor: عن ابن نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ ورفعنا لك ذكرك ﴾ قال لا أذكر إلا ذكرت معي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet forbids excessive praise like the Christians' praise of Jesus and instructs people to call him God's servant and messenger.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن عمر ابن الخطاب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا تطروني كما أطرت النصارى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says that after finishing prayer one should devote oneself to supplication.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ فإذا فرغت فانصب ﴾ قال فإذا فرغت من صلاتك فانصب في الدعاء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the verse addresses the human created in the best form and asks what can then make him deny the Judgment.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ فما يكذبك بعد بالدين ﴾ قال إنما يعني الإنسان يقول خلقتك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda would answer ‘yes’ and testify when reciting, ‘Is God not the wisest of judges?’
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق قال معمر وكان قتادة إذا تلا ﴿ أليس الله بأحكم الحاكمين ﴾ قال بلى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās would answer ‘yes’ when reciting the question whether God can revive the dead.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان إذا قرأ ﴿ أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى ﴾ قال بلى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet answered ‘yes’ after reciting this verse and also gave responses to other rhetorical questions in recitation.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ ﴿ فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون ﴾ قال آمنت بالله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Abū Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying; people called Abū Jahl the Pharaoh of this community.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ﴾ قال قال أبو جهل لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet said angels would seize Abū Jahl if he acted on his threat to trample the praying Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ سندع الزبانية ﴾ قال قال أبو جهل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses nādī as the man's living people or clan.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فليدع ناديه ﴾ قال قومه حية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says zabāniya is the Arabic word for the police.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ الزبانية ﴾ قال الزبانية في كلام العرب الشرط

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Reports from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār and al-Zuhrī say the first revelation came to the Prophet at Ḥirāʾ on a silk cloth bearing the opening of this sūra through ‘what he did not know.’
rows.anchor: عن معمر قال أخبرني عمرو بن دينار والزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says this was the first sūra revealed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن دينار قال سمعت عبيد بن عمير يقول أول سورة أنزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating and glosses the command as ‘prostrate and draw near.’
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months without a Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ خير من ألف شهر ﴾ قال خير من ألف شهر ليس فيها ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets Laylat al-Qadr as the Night of Judgment or decree.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر ﴾ قال في ليلة الحكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says worship through fasting and standing in prayer on that night surpasses a thousand months without it.
rows.anchor: قال الثوري وقال مجاهد صيامها وقيامها أفضل من صيام ألف شهر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says what will occur in the coming year is decreed that night until the next such night.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ من كل أمر سلام هي ﴾ قال تقضى فيها ما يكون في السنة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses salām here as goodness lasting until dawn.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ سلام هي ﴾ قال خير هي حتى مطلع الفجر

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة
rows.claim: Abū Qilāba says Laylat al-Qadr should be sought during the last ten nights.
rows.anchor: عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة قال ليلة القدر تتفقد في العشر الأواخر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains munfakkīn as coming to an end or ceasing from their present state.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ منفكين ﴾ قال منتهين عما هم فيه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When these verses were revealed, al-Ḥasan says a Muslim man took their warning to mean that even a speck of good or evil would be shown to him and accepted the admonition.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال لما نزلت ﴿ فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره ﴾

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A man learning the verses said that was enough for him; the Prophet said to leave him because he had understood.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دفع رجلا إلى رجل يعلمه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When a man covered his head in shame as the Prophet recited, the Prophet said that man had believed.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأها فقام رجل فجعل يضع يده

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says believers see their good deeds in the afterlife, while unbelievers see theirs in this world.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب أنه قال في قوله ﴿ فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ﴾ فقال أما المؤمن

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar asks pilgrims which verse is wisest, fairest, greatest, most hopeful, and most fearsome; they cite these verses as wisest, then cite 16:90, 2:255, 39:53, and 4:123 for the others.
rows.anchor: أن عمر بن الخطاب مر به ركب فأرسل إليهم يسألهم من هم فقالوا جئنا من الفج العميق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses al-khayr, ‘good,’ as wealth.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال ﴿ لحب الخير ﴾ هو المال

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says al-ʿihn is wool.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ كالعهن ﴾ قال هو الصوف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the certain knowledge mentioned here is death.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ علم اليقين ﴾ قال كنا نتحدث أنه الموت

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say people are not questioned about three necessities: clothes to cover themselves, a morsel to sustain them, and a home sheltering them from heat and cold.
rows.anchor: وكان الحسن وقتادة يقولان ثلاث لا يسأل عنهن ابن آدم وما خلاهن فيه المسألة والحساب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When people asked whether dates and water count as the bounty about which they will be questioned, the Prophet answered that this would indeed be so.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي الزبير قال لما نزلت ﴿ ثم لتسألن يومئذ عن النعيم ﴾ قالوا يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the slanderer attacks with tongue and eye, consumes people's flesh, and criticizes them.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ويل لكل همزة ﴾ قال يهمزه ويلمزه بلسانه وعينه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses muʾṣada as shut or sealed over.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ مؤصدة ﴾ قال مطبقة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the extended columns are instruments with which people are punished in the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ عمد ممددة ﴾ قال عمد يعذبون بها في النار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda describes the birds as numerous and arriving in succession.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ طيرا أبابيل ﴾ قال طيرا كثيرا متتابعة

rows.speaker: عمران
rows.claim: ʿImrān describes numerous birds carrying numerous stones, the largest like a chickpea and the smallest like a lentil.
rows.anchor: عن موسى بن أبي عائشة عن عمران في قوله تعالى ﴿ طيرا أبابيل ﴾ قال طيرا كثيرة جاءت

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the stones of sijjīl were made of clay.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ بحجارة من سجيل ﴾ قال هي من طين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the birds came from the sea, each carrying three stones, and each stone shattered whatever it struck.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ طيرا أبابيل ﴾ قال خرجت من قبل البحر بيض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says each stone raised a lesion on an attacker, the first occurrence of smallpox; a flood then swept them into the sea.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال لما أرسل الله الحجارة على أصحاب الفيل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the eaten chaff as straw.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ كعصف مأكول ﴾ قال هو التبن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Quraysh's familiar custom was a winter journey and a summer journey.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لإيلاف قريش ﴾ قال عادة قريش عادتهم رحلة الشتاء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī specifies their winter journey went to Yemen and their summer journey to Syria.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق قال معمر وقال الكلبي كانت لهم رحلتان رحلة في الشتاء إلى اليمن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Quraysh were safe in pre-Islamic times because they belonged to God's sanctuary, while other Arab tribes were raided when they traveled.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وآمنهم من خوف ﴾ قال كانوا يقولون نحن من حرم الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains that the denier shoves, oppresses, and wrongs the orphan.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يدع اليتيم ﴾ قال يقهره ويظلمه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they neglect prayer and do not care whether they prayed.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون ﴾ قال ساه عنها لا يبالي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet identified al-Kawthar as a river in Paradise whose banks have pearl domes, shown to him by Gabriel.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس بن مالك في قوله تعالى ﴿ إنا أعطيناك الكوثر ﴾ أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال هو نهر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the commanded prayer as the Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فصل لربك وانحر ﴾ قال هي صلاة الأضحى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the command to sacrifice refers to sacrificial camels.
rows.anchor: قال معمر وقال قتادة نحر البدن لقوله وانحر

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib interprets the command as placing the right hand over the left during prayer.
rows.anchor: عن عاصم الجحدري عن عقبة بن ظهير عن علي بن أبي طالب في قوله تعالى ﴿ فصل لربك وانحر ﴾

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
rows.claim: Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ say to pray the dawn prayer at Muzdalifa and sacrifice the camels at Minā.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد وفطر عن عطاء في قوله ﴿ فصل لربك وانحر ﴾ قالا صل الصبح

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the Prophet's enemy as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who called Muhammad cut off because he had no surviving son; God says the enemy is the one cut off.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ إن شانئك هو الأبتر ﴾ قال هو العاص بن وائل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses abtar as contemptible, slight, and humiliated.
rows.anchor: قال معمر وقال قتادة الأبتر الحقير الدقيق الذليل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says this sūra is equivalent to a quarter of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال ﴿ قل يا أيها الكافرون ﴾ تعدل ربع القرآن

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Quraysh offered to follow the Prophet for a year if he would return to their religion for a year, and this sūra was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم الأحول قال سمعت وهبا يقول قالت كفار قريش للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reflects that the Prophet's appointed time was brought near after the promised victory, and thanks God for granting him joy and hastening his honor.
rows.anchor: عن معمر عن الحسن قال كان إذا قرأ ﴿ إذا جاء نصر الله والفتح ﴾ قال احتسب رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the sūra marked the limit God set for the Prophet and announced he would live only a short time after Mecca's conquest.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة أن ابن عباس قال في قوله تعالى ﴿ إذا جاء نصر الله والفتح ﴾ إلى آخرها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying Yemenis have the softest hearts and that faith, understanding, and wisdom are Yemeni.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين قال سمعت أبا هريرة يقول لنا نزلت ﴿ إذا جاء نصر الله ﴾ قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When the sūra was revealed, the Prophet announced the victory, the opening, and the arrival of Yemenis, praising their tender hearts, obedience, faith, understanding, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال لما نزلت ﴿ إذا جاء نصر الله ﴾ قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جاء نصر الله وجاء الفتح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In response to ʿUmar's question, Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the opening as Mecca's conquest, the people entering in groups, and the Prophet's command to glorify God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن عمر دعا نفرا من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسألهم عن ﴿ إذا جاء نصر الله والفتح ﴾

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Abū Lahab's hands were ruined and he himself was ruined.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ تبت يدا أبي لهب ﴾ قال خسرت يدا أبي لهب وخسر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets carrying firewood as carrying words through gossip.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وامرأته حمالة الحطب ﴾ قال كانت تحطب الكلام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An unnamed group says she taunted the Prophet for poverty and actually carried wood, so the verse rebukes her by both meanings.
rows.anchor: قال معمر وقال بعضهم كانت تعير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالفقر وكانت تحطب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says what Abū Lahab earned refers to his children.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة عن ابن عباس قال وما كسب قال هم الولد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the cord of twisted fiber was a necklace made of cowrie shells.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ حبل من مسد ﴾ قال قلادة من ودع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses al-ṣamad as the everlasting one.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال ﴿ الصمد ﴾ الدائم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says al-ṣamad is the one with no hollow.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق قال معمر وقال عكرمة هو الذي لا جوف له

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid also says al-ṣamad is the one with no hollow.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال الصمد الذي لا جوف له

rows.speaker: شقيق
rows.claim: Shaqīq says al-ṣamad is the master who has reached the utmost degree of mastery.
rows.anchor: عن عاصم عن شقيق قال الصمد السيد الذي قد انتهى في سؤدده

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies al-falaq as daybreak.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ الفلق ﴾ قال هو فلق الصبح

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says ghāsiq refers to when darkness comes in and enters among people.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ غاسق إذا وقب ﴾ قال إذا أقبل إذا دخل على الناس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda instead explains it as when the darkness goes away or sets.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة إذا غاب إذا ذهب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda warns against incantations mixed with magic.
rows.anchor: قال معمر تلا قتادة ﴿ ومن شر النفاثات في العقد ﴾ قال إياكم وما خالط السحر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says whoever consults a soothsayer and believes him has disbelieved what was revealed to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة عن هبيرة عن ابن مسعود قال من أتى كاهنا فسأله وصدقه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the evil to seek refuge from is the evil eye and the self; ʿAṭāʾ reports the same gloss.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ومن شر حاسد إذا حسد ﴾ قال من شر عينه ونفسه

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Ṭāwūs says the evil eye is real and may precede destiny; he describes a washing ritual for the person who caused it, whose water is then poured over the afflicted person.
rows.anchor: قال معمر وسمعت ابن طاوس يحدث عن أبيه قال العين حق

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Ṭāwūs says the incantations closest to associating partners with God are those for a snakebite and for madness.
rows.anchor: عن معمر عن ابن طاوس عن أبيه قال أقرب الرقى إلى الشرك رقية الحية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the whisperer is Satan, also called the retreating one: he whispers and withdraws when God is remembered.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ الوسواس ﴾ قال هو الشيطان وهو الخناس أيضا إذا ذكر الله خنس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says devils exist among humans and jinn, so refuge is sought from both groups.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ من الجنة والناس ﴾ قال إن من الناس شياطين ومن الجن شياطين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says every newborn has a whisperer at the heart; it withdraws when God is remembered and whispers when the person is heedless.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال ما من مولود إلا وعلى قلبه وسواس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda describes the retreating whisperer as having a dog's snout and whispering into human breasts until remembrance makes it withdraw.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال يقال الخناس له خرطوم كخرطوم الكلب يوسوس في صدور الإنسان

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports that the Prophet told him the two protective sūras were given to him to recite, and that they recite as he did.
rows.anchor: عن زر بن حبيش قال سألت أبي بن كعب عن المعوذتين فقال سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عنهما

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: In another report, Ubayy says the Prophet was told to say the two refuge sūras, and they say as he said.
rows.anchor: عن عاصم عن زر بن حبيش قال سألت أبي بن كعب عن المعوذتين

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir reports that the Prophet recited Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ and the two refuge sūras and said no one had sought refuge with anything like them.
rows.anchor: عن الثوري من جهينة عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ قال

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: A second report from ʿUqba says verses unparalleled in what was heard or seen were revealed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن الثوري عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد عن قيس عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني قال قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
